question: Can ReprForge discharge a changed processor-file fingerprint with a compact, exact, collection-scoped output certificate, and what CPU cost does that proof add to a version transition?

measurement.source_fingerprint: One-time source-build work: image decode, source processing, and streaming output hashing.
measurement.target_certificate: Update-time work: image decode, target processing, streaming output hashing, and digest comparison. No model or GPU execution.
measurement.comparison: The target processor scan is also required by a raw rebuild. Report it separately from hashing/certificate metadata; do not compare the entire scan directly with GPU-only model timings.

gates.exact_equivalence: Source and target ordered output digests, field contracts, item counts, and scope fingerprints are identical.
gates.coverage: All 2,225 pages in the three frozen corpus shards are processed.
gates.compact_proof: Serialized source output fingerprint plus transition certificate is <= 4096 bytes.
gates.negative_control: A one-bit digest change is rejected by certificate construction.
gates.gpu: No CUDA context and no GPU model execution.

claim_boundary: Collection-scoped processor-output equivalence for this exact ordered corpus and batch schedule. It does not prove global processor equivalence or make ColPali compact IR deployable.
